# Internationalization

Implementation: `src/i18n/`. Tooling: `scripts/i18n-audit.js`, `scripts/i18n-build-locale.js`.

| Fact              | Value                                          |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| Languages         | 30, listed in `src/i18n/languages.ts`          |
| Source language   | `en`, 1,528 strings + 27 plural keys           |
| Catalog           | `src/i18n/locales/<code>.ts`, flat dotted keys |
| Hardcoded strings | 0, enforced by `i18n:audit -- --max 0`         |
| Adding a language | one JSON map + one line; see below             |

## The Rule

Never write a user-facing string inline. Add a key to `src/i18n/locales/en.ts` and use `T("your.key")` in a component or `t("your.key")` outside React.

The catalog is what makes every string greppable, reviewable in one diff, and consistent in wording.

## File Layout

| Path                        | Holds                                                          |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `src/i18n/index.ts`         | `t` / `useT` / `tPlural`, the catalog registry, the RTL policy |
| `src/i18n/languages.ts`     | the language table: endonym, direction, script                 |
| `src/i18n/plurals.ts`       | CLDR category selection, and which forms each language needs   |
| `src/i18n/layout.ts`        | RTL helpers React Native has no logical form for               |
| `src/i18n/locales/en.ts`    | the source catalog, hand-written                               |
| `src/i18n/locales/types.ts` | `TranslationKey` and `PluralKey`, derived from `en.ts`         |
| `src/utils/message-text.ts` | resolves a stored row's `systemKey` at render                  |

## Completeness Is a Type

Every locale is annotated `Strings`, which is `Record<TranslationKey, string>` derived from `en.ts`. A locale missing a key does not compile, so there is no runtime fallback and no coverage threshold.

Adding an English key breaks every incomplete locale at compile time rather than degrading it in front of a user.

## Plurals

Use `tPlural`. Never concatenate.

```ts
tPlural("mesh.peers_in_range", count); // correct
`${n} peer${n !== 1 ? "s" : ""} in range`; // wrong
```

Selection lives in `src/i18n/plurals.ts`. Hermes has no `Intl.PluralRules`, and across these thirty languages there are only nine distinct CLDR shapes, so the rules are hand-written rather than polyfilled. `plurals.test.ts` checks every rule against Node's ICU for every integer 0 to 2000.

`PLURAL_CATEGORIES` says which forms each language needs, and `catalog.test.ts` holds every catalog to exactly that set. This matters because `PluralForms` makes every category except `other` optional, so a Russian catalog carrying only `one` and `other` type-checks and reads "5 сообщение" from five up.

## Placeholders

Named (`{count}`, `{name}`), never positional. Translators reorder sentences; a named placeholder survives that.

For a sentence with a link inside it, use `useRichText`. Do not concatenate `<Text>` fragments.

## Never Translate at Module Load or Storage

```ts
const SCOPES = { tag: t("chat.scope.mesh") }; // wrong: frozen at import
const SCOPES = { tagKey: "chat.scope.mesh" }; // correct
```

Same bug one level in: a `useMemo` calling `t()` with only `[Colors]` in its deps never recomputes on a language change. Use the `T` from `useT()` inside the memo and list it. `npm run i18n:audit` fails the build on both shapes.

A row written into MMKV is the third shape. `t()` at write time bakes a language into storage, so persisted rows carry a `systemKey` and translate on render through `messageText()`.

## What Not to Translate

These cross the wire or derive an identity. `catalog.test.ts` enforces the list.

| Thing                               | Where                                    | Why                                                                                                        |
| ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Adjective and noun word lists       | `src/utils/username.ts`                  | Identity derivation. One peer resolves to one name everywhere and in bitchat                               |
| Transmitted `/hug` and `/slap` text | `message-thread.tsx`                     | bitchat matches the English substrings                                                                     |
| Slash command tokens                | `/hug`, `/who`, `/msg`, `/pay`           | The parser matches them. Translate the hint instead                                                        |
| Channel names and geohashes         | `#bluetooth`, cell ids                   | Protocol identifiers, verbatim inside translated prose                                                     |
| Proper nouns                        | Airhop, Nostr, Cashu, Lightning, Tor     | `Lightning` and `Tor` are ordinary words in most languages and will be translated unless the test stops it |
| Nicknames, group names, notices     | everywhere                               | User content                                                                                               |
| Licence texts                       | `src/data/licenses.ts`                   | Quoted verbatim                                                                                            |
| Terms and Privacy clauses           | `terms-screen.tsx`, `privacy-screen.tsx` | English is authoritative                                                                                   |
| Mint and relay error strings        | wallet, nostr                            | Authored by a remote server                                                                                |

## Right to Left

Arabic, Persian and Urdu. The other twenty-seven share English's direction.

- Logical properties only: `marginStart`, `paddingStart`, `borderTopStartRadius`. Never the physical forms; an eslint rule enforces this.
- `textAlign` has no logical end value in React Native. Use `textAlignEnd` from `layout.ts`, and `"auto"` for the leading edge.
- Directional glyphs do not mirror. Use `chevronForward`, `chevronBack`, `arrowBack`. `arrow-up-right` means outward and stays put.
- `radar-view.tsx` must never mirror. It is a polar plot of physical space, and it is exempt from the eslint rule for that reason.
- A header title needs `flexGrow` as well as `flexShrink`, or it ellipsizes with free space beside it.
- Direction is fixed at process start, so choosing an RTL language applies on the next launch. `initI18n()` pins it.

## Commands

| Command                          | Does                                                                   |
| -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `npm run i18n:audit`             | hardcoded strings, worst file first. Also fails on frozen translations |
| `npm run i18n:audit -- --list`   | every hit with a line number                                           |
| `npm run i18n:audit -- --unused` | catalog keys nothing references                                        |
| `npm run i18n:audit -- --max 0`  | CI: fail if any hardcoded string is added                              |

## Adding a Language

Two steps.

1. Write the translation as a flat `{ key: text }` JSON map, plus a `plurals` map carrying exactly the CLDR categories the language uses. Then:

   ```bash
   node scripts/i18n-build-locale.js <code> <translations.json>
   ```

   It reads `en.ts` for key order and section markers, and writes nothing unless every key is present, no key is extra, no string is empty, placeholders match English, plural categories are right, protocol tokens are carried through verbatim, proper nouns survive, and no character belongs to a script the language does not write in. The emitted file is a normal hand-editable catalog from then on.

2. Add one line to `CATALOGS` in `index.ts`, with its import. The picker, `LANGUAGE_ORDER`, plural selection and `catalog.test.ts` all derive from it.

Then `npx prettier --write` the new file and run `npm test`.

Still outstanding per language: generated `InfoPlist.strings` for the iOS permission dialogs, and `values-<code>/strings.xml` for the Android foreground-service notification. Both are selected by device language rather than app language.

## What Not to Do

- Write a user-facing string inline.
- Pluralise with `n === 1 ? "" : "s"` at a call site.
- Call `t()` at module scope, inside a memo without the translator in its deps, or when writing to a store.
- Use `marginLeft`, `left`, or `textAlign: "right"` in a stylesheet.
- Translate anything in the table above.
- Set translated prose in `FontFamily.mono`. JetBrains Mono carries no Arabic, Devanagari or Han glyphs. Mono is for machine data.
- Ship a language whose catalog is not complete.
